design.concept: A decision-first inbox for the manager: the page opens on the volume waiting for a decision (one big number with the main action) and, right below, a board of cards, one per pending expense. Each card opens with a full-width status strip, shows who registered it and the amount large, and one click on it goes straight to the analysis of that expense.
design.decisions: One view, no scene host: the page has a single intent (navigate to the analysis) and no state of its own, so a drawer would need page state the contract forbids. The decision is made on the team-expenses page, so the card itself is the one-click outcome. I kept the template's board of cards (card-grid, no table), the full-width status strip at the top of each card (warning tone and 'resubmitted after correction' when the expense was resubmitted, info tone for plain waiting), and the amount and date as the large decisive values. The header pairs the big-number metric (totalPendentes straight from the backend) with the primary button, which opens the first pending expense on the board. Loading, error with retry and empty (large icon, one sentence, reload) are designed. A 'load more' button appears only when the list reports more pages. Values are only formatted (Intl), never computed.
